figmaBuildPlan.tokenProfileHint: marketing theme with dark hero, Sora headings, Inter body, bold accent CTA, logo-led trust bar, text-first product modules, compact gallery for images and videos, simple card-based pricing and testimonial patterns

sections.variantHint: dark-centered-left-content, no large hero media, logo slot present, compact value bullets, primary CTA + ghost secondary CTA
sections.notes: Use dark theme hero with white text. Apply Sora for headline and Inter for supporting copy. Headline size should follow 16+ word rule at 36px/600. Include a left-aligned brand/logo slot. Keep CTA cluster compact with primary solid accent button and secondary outline button even if secondary CTA text is empty; use contextual label 'Request Demo' only if needed in hero component variant. Include a short bullet-value list derived from supporting line and extras. No prominent media block in hero.

sections.variantHint: logo-led trust strip with brand chips and supporting proof line
sections.contentSource: context.additionalInstructions + Techjockey design memory trustSignals + contentMap.trust
sections.notes: This section must be dominated by logos as the primary trust signal. Since no logos are supplied in contentMap, reserve logo chip slots as placeholders for partner/customer logos and use Techjockey trust signals as supporting microcopy: 1,00,000+ businesses, Genuine licenses, Free implementation support, Best price guaranteed. Keep this section visually compact and immediately after hero. Use a light grey or very dark separator panel depending on final contrast review, but maintain logo prominence.

sections.variantHint: mixed media gallery with image tiles and video preview tiles, dark theme compatible
sections.notes: Create a gallery section containing both images and videos, as requested. Use a clean grid of compact rectangular cards with 2-3 featured media tiles and supporting caption rows. Media should represent AI image generation and AI video generation outcomes. Keep it utility-first and not decorative. Include short labels such as 'AI Images', 'AI Video Outputs', 'Multimodal Creation'.

sections.variantHint: text-led feature module with compact feature grid
sections.notes: Stacked product module for Seedream 4.5. Use a strong section title, product label, descriptive paragraph, and a 5-item feature grid. Since there are 5 features, render as a 3-column grid on desktop with responsive wrap. Use white card containers on a dark page with clear contrast or a deep elevated panel if the overall page uses dark sectioning. Include CTA 'Request Demo' in the module footer.

sections.variantHint: text-led feature module with compact feature grid
sections.notes: Stacked product module for Seedance 1.5 Pro. Use the 5 feature list in a 3-column desktop grid. Keep the description concise and emphasize synchronized audio-visual generation, lip-sync, cinematic control, and speed. No CTA text is provided in the source, so render the module without a button unless the section template requires a standard tertiary CTA slot.

sections.variantHint: two-card pricing/quote layout, simple card style, no comparison table
sections.notes: Use two simple plan cards aligned to the page’s lead-gen pattern. One plan has a price only for Seedance 1.5 Pro; the other is quote-based. Include the includes checklist on each card and a full-width 'Get Quote' CTA. Avoid heavy pricing-table complexity.

sections.variantHint: 3-column testimonial cards with star row and italic quote
sections.notes: Render five testimonials as 3-column grid on desktop, wrapping to second row. Include gold star rating, italic quote, bold author name, and grey designation. Use accent left border per design memory. Keep cards compact and highly readable.

Add a minimal footer area only. Keep it utility-focused with compliance/support links, cart reference if needed, and a short closing line. Do not introduce new marketing content. Use dark theme-consistent footer treatment.

sections.variantHint: stacked text-only hero, no large media, compact CTA stack
sections.notes: Mobile hero must stack cleanly. Keep logo slot, headline, subheadline, supporting line, and CTA stack. Primary CTA full-width and first; secondary CTA full-width below if used. Reduce copy density and maintain strong dark-theme contrast.

sections.variantHint: horizontal logo strip with overflow-scroll if needed
sections.notes: Preserve logo-led trust on mobile. Use a horizontally scrollable row of logo chips or compact logo placeholders, followed by a short row of trust signals. Avoid wrapping that increases height too much.

sections.variantHint: single-column media stack with one video tile and two image tiles
sections.notes: On mobile, stack gallery tiles in a single column. One video preview tile first, followed by image tiles. Keep captions short. Ensure media remains constrained and does not overpower the primary CTA path.

Convert feature grid to a single column on mobile. Keep description first, then five feature cards or accordion rows if space efficiency is needed. CTA may be placed at the bottom as a full-width button.
Convert the Seedance feature set to a single vertical list with concise row cards. Keep the copy compact and preserve the emphasis on synchronized audio-video generation and fast inference.

Render pricing as stacked full-width cards. Make CTAs full-width and maintain checklist readability. If price text is sparse, use whitespace intelligently while keeping quote-based card clearly separated.
Stack testimonials in a single column, preserving star rating, italic quote, and author meta. Keep card height compact and support vertical scrolling if necessary.
Keep footer minimal and vertical on mobile. Limit to essential links and closing utility content only.

figmaExecutionNotes: Use a dark theme throughout with high-contrast typography and accent CTA color; do not use a white hero.
Make logos the dominant trust signal in the trust section and keep it immediately after hero.
Preserve the linear flow: hero, trust logos, gallery, Seedream product, Seedance product, pricing, testimonials, footer.
Use design-system cards with minimal ornament, 12px radius, 24px padding, and consistent 8/12/16/24/32 spacing tokens.
Treat gallery as a distinct section with both image and video tiles; keep it compact and utility-first.
On desktop, use 3-column feature and testimonial grids; on mobile, collapse all grids to single-column stacks.
Keep CTA repetition contextual at section level and avoid adding unsupported sections such as forms or news.

accentVisuals: floating spec chips for 4K image / synchronized audio-video / text-to-video
masonry-style mini gallery of AI stills and cinematic thumbnails
enterprise logo band beneath the hero fold
heroStrategy.headline: Create High-Quality AI Images & Videos with ByteDance Generative Models
heroStrategy.subheadline: Unlock next-generation generative AI with Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro — advanced ByteDance foundation models for premium image creation, editing, and synchronized video generation.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use an unexpected cinematic editorial hero: full-width orange-to-dark mesh background with a strong left text column and a right-side layered media workspace built from floating UI cards rather than a single image. Keep the hero premium and enterprise-ready with glassmorphism panels, subtle grid lines, orange accent glow, and dark contrast. Make the visual system feel like a creative AI studio: image samples, video thumbnail cards, waveform/timeline cues, and logo-led trust architecture. CTAs must be solid orange, with the primary button dominant and the secondary button outlined. Avoid centered text and avoid generic split-hero repetition; the composition should feel more like a sophisticated launch page than a standard SaaS template.

repetitionBreakers: Use a vivid orange hero with layered visual mockups, then switch immediately to a dark trust band for contrast.
Make the first product block a spotlight-plus-grid image module, and the second a split-panel video module.
Insert a light-background proof or testimonial break between dark sections to avoid tonal monotony.
Keep CTA cadence contextual: hero, product blocks, pricing, and final form, all using the same CTA text.
blueprint.pageTitle: Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro | AI Image and Video Generation
blueprint.metaDescription: Create high-quality AI images and videos with ByteDance models Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro. Explore image generation, video generation, proof, pricing, and a simple Get started path.

sections.backgroundTreatment: bold brand-orange field with floating-orb depth, subtle grain, and layered preview frames
sections.designNote: Visual-dominant but still content-first enough to answer what this is, who it is for, and what to do next. Keep the left side crisp and conversion-led with the headline 'Create High-Quality AI Images & Videos with ByteDance Generative Models', a supporting subheadline for creative, marketing, design, and video teams, and a single solid orange Get started CTA. On the right, show stacked image and video generation previews, prompt-to-output cards, and small chips for image, video, and audio-visual creation.

Place trust early and keep it prominent because trustStrategy is logos-first. Use 3-6 recognizable enterprise/creative logos in a high-contrast horizontal band. If fewer than 3 logos are available, replace with a metric strip, but prioritize logos here. Keep this section compact and immediate after the hero.

featurePresentation.primaryFeatureTitle: How it works in under 60 seconds

sections.designNote: This section should satisfy the warm-traffic sequence before deeper proof. Present a 3-step flow: 1) enter a prompt, 2) choose image or video model, 3) generate and refine. Use a clean light surface for contrast against the dark hero and trust bar. Keep copy minimal and scannable, with one preview panel showing prompt-to-output. Make the rhythm instructional, not salesy.

Use a logo-led proof band first if logos exist, then layer in testimonial content as supporting credibility. Since proof type is logos, foreground the recognisable brand strip and use testimonial quotes as secondary validation. Keep the section visually richer than the previous one, with a dark editorial backdrop and a compact proof headline that signals enterprise confidence.

Lead with Seedream 4.5 because the click intent is likely image quality and creative control. Use a spotlight-plus-grid layout with a dominant visual preview on one side and the most important 4-5 features on the other: text-image alignment, 1K-4K output, typographic rendering, multi-image composition, and structural fidelity. This section should feel like an interactive creative workspace rather than a generic feature list.

The second product block must feel different from the first. Use a dark cinematic panel with an accordion or expanding feature stack for Seedance 1.5 Pro. Prioritize text-to-video, audio-visual synchronization, multilingual lip-sync, cinematic camera control, and 10x faster inference. Include a preview strip with video frames and waveform overlays to make the product feel alive.

Keep pricing simple, utility-first, and aligned with the lead-gen layout. Use two clear plan cards or a compact comparison table for Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro. Emphasize what's included rather than discounting. Place a single solid orange Get started CTA on each plan, but keep the overall section restrained to avoid CTA fatigue.

Since there are 5 testimonials, show them as a 3-card grid with optional carousel behavior on smaller screens. Keep the cards editorial and premium, with prominent quotes from creative, video, and marketing leaders. Alternate card treatments subtly so adjacent sections do not feel visually repeated.

End with a high-energy conversion block that echoes the hero but feels more direct. Use a centered floating card on the orange field, with one concise message and a single full-width mobile CTA labeled Get started. This should feel like the easiest next step: see it in action, not sign up for a generic account.
If additional brand or media proof is available, place it as a minimal utility footer-like logo strip. Keep it quiet and unobtrusive, preserving the primary conversion momentum above.

blueprint.designPersonality: A premium AI studio for serious creative teams: bold, dark, intelligent, and logo-led. The page should feel like enterprise software meets cinematic content lab, with strong contrast, orange brand energy, glassy cards, and proof-first trust architecture.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use a premium creative-campaign aesthetic with layered AI image samples, cinematic video thumbnails, waveform overlays, prompt-to-output preview cards, and floating spec chips. Include a dedicated gallery section featuring both videos and still images in a masonry or asymmetrical grid, using dark framing, subtle glow edges, and UI shell overlays to simulate an intelligent generation workspace.

typography.heroFontSizeReason: The headline is long and detailed, so a smaller hero size keeps it balanced while preserving hierarchy on a dark premium layout.

colours.colourReason: The brand palette already defines orange, white, black, and light grey. The hero and primary CTA should use the brand orange exactly, with the dark neutral brand base as the page background to create premium contrast and a distinct Techjockey identity.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Single-screen top hero with left-aligned brand/logo slot, strong H1, short supporting paragraph, and a compact bullet-value list below; no prominent hero media in the reference. Primary conversion is pushed into the hero/form adjacency rather than a large hero CTA cluster.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Linear landing-page flow: hero/banner, lead-capture form block, then stacked product detail sections. Sections are separated by clear vertical breaks and modest contrast changes rather than heavy decoration.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Simple content cards with strong hierarchy, minimal ornament, rectangular containers, and utility-first information density. Emphasis is on readable copy blocks and feature lists over decorative card treatments.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Primary CTA-led conversion model with one dominant action in hero and secondary request/demo action inside product modules. CTA placement is contextual and repeated at section level rather than persistent global navigation.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No observable pricing module in the reference pattern; if added, it should use simple plan cards or table-like blocks aligned with the page’s lead-gen layout.
referenceMap.footerMode: Not represented in the extracted reference structure; assume a minimal utility footer with compliance/support links if needed.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Mostly text-first layout with optional small brand/logo imagery; media is secondary and should be constrained to compact placements or support panels, not full-width immersive visuals.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Stacked product sections with a label/eyebrow, headline, descriptive paragraph, then feature list items. Each section can repeat the same module pattern for multiple offerings, supporting progressive disclosure by feature grouping.
referenceMap.formPattern: Dedicated lead form panel placed directly after the hero. Uses a boxed card treatment, clear heading, stacked fields, and hidden tracking inputs. Best suited for high-intent conversion pages.
referenceMap.animationStyle: Static, low-motion landing page styling with no clear animation dependency; interaction is primarily through form submission and standard page navigation.
designNotes: Use compact, high-clarity copy blocks with strong typographic hierarchy.
Keep feature lists scannable and repeatable across products.
Use the form as a primary module, not an afterthought.
Maintain strong whitespace and restrained visual noise.
If media is added, keep it supportive and secondary to the value proposition.

PROOF STRATEGY: The visitor trusts logos most. Make this the dominant trust signal.

use dark theme, Create gallery section containing videos and images in the landing page

mustHaveMoments: Dark-theme hero with strong headline and concise value proposition
Logos-first trust band placed immediately below the hero to establish credibility
Dedicated gallery section showcasing both AI images and AI videos with motion-friendly previews
Separate product detail blocks for Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro with clear capability differentiation
Pricing/quote cards with strong conversion prompts and repeated section-level CTAs
Testimonials positioned after product proof to reinforce decision confidence
Minimal utility footer for support and compliance
avoidPatterns: Large unstructured hero media that delays message comprehension
Badge-only trust presentation without recognizable company logos
Overly decorative visuals that reduce technical credibility
Long-form paragraphs in place of scannable feature lists
Persistent global navigation competing with the main conversion path
Mixing both products into one indistinct feature block
designStrategy.reasoning: This page should behave like a high-intent lead-generation landing page for solution-aware professionals who already understand AI content creation and need proof plus clarity. The dominant trust signal must be logos-first, so the layout should prioritize a logo strip or client/partner proof band near the top, followed by a direct product-led message. A split hero is best for balancing concise copy with immediate visual credibility, while a dark theme will make the generative AI positioning feel premium and modern. Because the brief specifically asks for a gallery section containing videos and images, that moment should act as a proof-rich showcase between the hero/trust area and the deeper product sections. CTA language should remain strong and repeated, since the goal is lead capture and demo/quote requests rather than passive awareness.

strengths: Design planned from strategy and intent layers
